title: Define always_free versus recurring_quota
objective: Define a decision-complete, evidence-based boundary between always_free and recurring_quota that provider authors and evaluators can apply consistently without changing classifier, provider, schema, fixture, or web behavior.
in_scope: docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md only to correct wording made false by the fail-closed offer-type classifier
out_of_scope_zero_diff: apps/api/app/models/vocab.py and all classifier or publication code
provider configs, profiles, fixtures, and provider documentation
promotion or merge of the draft pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1: DATA_MODEL defines always_free and recurring_quota with an exclusive, source-evidence-based decision rule that two independent provider authors can apply to the same offer.
A2: The recommendation evaluates a real semantic split, preserving recurring allowances under always_free, and removal from the vocabulary.
A3: At least three merged real offers are walked through the selected rule, and every merged Cloudflare and GitHub production profile is accounted for.
A4: Existing precedent and any reclassification blast radius are quantified, but no provider data is changed.
A5: The documentation states that both offer types are currently classifier-neutral, Z0-eligible, and absent from TEMPORARY_CONDITIONAL_OFFER_TYPES, so the selected label alone changes no Z0 verdict.
A6: The public Recurring quota filter consequence is disclosed.
A7: The documentation states that the boundary is an author/evaluator contract, not machine-enforced semantic validation.

A8: Removal blast radius covers the canonical vocabulary, both database CHECK constraints and a migration, the web filter, adviser fixtures/tests, and persisted offer and immutable offer-version rows.
A9: URL allowlist and Prettier checks pass, draft PR CI has all five checks green, and the pull request remains draft.
A10: The diff is limited to approved files; progress.md is a strict base-prefix append ending in LF.
verification_plan: Measure all recurring_quota and always_free references and parse merged provider expected fixtures.
Run the canonical repository test/check commands, including Prettier and the URL allowlist.
Run a fresh documentation rubric review against the contract and diff.
Commit, push, open a draft pull request at the first pushed commit, wait for all five CI checks, and inspect PR state.
Immediately before reporting, re-derive origin/main with git ls-remote and pull request state with gh pr view.
negative_tests: A quota reset cadence alone must not force recurring_quota when the allowance belongs to an explicitly zero-priced plan or tier.
A recurring grant attached to a paid or pay-as-you-go base account must not be called always_free merely because the grant renews.
When official evidence does not establish whether a zero-priced plan or only a recurring grant exists, authors must not guess between the two labels.
data_implications: Documentation only. No persisted row, migration, CHECK constraint, fixture, or provider classification changes in this slice.
security_privacy: No security, privacy, credential, network, or dependency change.
portability: Documentation and agent-state only; no runtime or platform behavior changes.
z0_risk: No runtime Z0 change. The classifier treats always_free and recurring_quota identically: both are recognized, neither is self-hosted or temporary/conditional, and either can reach Z0 only when all independent billing and exhaustion gates pass.
